podcast.body: Bob Dylan included his version of "House of the Rising Sun" on his first album, initially titled "Baby Let Me Fall You Down." He learned the song from Eric Von Schmidt and adapted Dave Van Ronk's arrangement, simplifying the chords. "Bob Dullin had in turn learned it from Vunsemit, and included it on his first album as Baby Let Me Fall You Down."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: Dylan's first album, recorded quickly in a couple of days, contained only two original songs. Producer John Hammond found Dylan difficult to work with due to his microphone technique and refusal to do second takes for many songs. The album was not a commercial success and was known within Columbia Records as "Hammond's folly," but it did not lose money due to its swift recording. Dylan and Hammond later spoke poorly of it, though it is regarded by some as one of the best outputs from the Greenwich Village folk scene. "Hammond's track record was good enough that he was allowed to get on with it and put out an album."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
